# Compare Options

> Compare real alternatives on the dimensions the decision actually turns on, and recommend one.

## Done means
- Dimensions are chosen from the decision, and each is weighted or marked as a hard requirement.
- Every option is scored on every dimension, with a note rather than a blank where information is missing.
- The cheapest and the do-nothing options appear, even when they are obviously wrong, because they set the baseline.
- Cost includes the cost of being wrong later — switching cost, lock-in, who has to learn it.
- The recommendation names one option, the decisive dimension, and what would change the answer.

## Output contract
```
## Decision
<what is being chosen, and by when, and what is at stake>
## Dimensions
| dimension | weight or hard requirement | why it matters here |
## Comparison
| dimension | option A | option B | option C | do nothing |
## Recommendation
<option> — <decisive reason> — <what would flip it>
## Reversibility
<what it costs to change course in six months>
```

## Gotchas
Do not pad the option list with strawmen. Do not let a numeric total decide; the table informs judgment, it does not replace it. Unknowns are findings, so list them rather than guessing a score.
